headline: Continued reviews of parking lot repaving at 231 Second Ave and new building at 234 Calvary Street to October 8, 2026.
summary: The Commission continued a Request for Determination of Applicability for 231 Second Ave and a Notice of Intent for 234 Calvary Street to the October 8 meeting. It also approved September 10 minutes, heard a CPC funding report, and discussed draft conservation restrictions for review.
decisions: Continued the Request for Determination of Applicability for 231 Second Ave to the October 8 meeting.
Continued the Notice of Intent for 234 Calvary Street (DEP File # 316-tba) to the October 8 meeting.
CPC approved $50,768 for First Parish Church steeple repairs.
CPC approved $104,600 for 20 Felton Street windows and siding replacement.
CPC approved $350,000 for restoration of 43 windows at Gore Place.

plain_text:
Approved 10-8-2026 
  
 
Waltham Conservation Commission 
September 24, 2026 
Meeting Minutes 
Meeting took place via public Zoom call with participation information posted at City Hall, Government 
Center, and on the Commission’s page of the city web site. Zoom information was circulated directly 
to all applicants and others on the public agenda. 
Meeting called to order at 7:04 PM. 
Attendees: Chair Bill Doyle, Gerard Dufromont, Michael Donovan, Frank Fitzgerald. Conservation 
Agent Julia Abbott. 
Absent: Vice Chair Lisa Limonciello, Anja Shafer. 
 
Public Meeting 
Request for Determination of Applicability (continued from 9-10-2026) 
Applicant: Devin McArthur 
Property Location: 231 Second Ave 
Project Description: Reclaim, grade, pave, and stripe 37,370 sq.ft. commercial parking lot. No 
change to the current parking lot dimensions, only reestablishing a solid gravel base and repaving. 
Ms. Abbott informed the commission that the applicant has asked to continue. They are still working 
with Cambridge Water, specifically on the O&M plan, and expect to be ready by the next meeting. Mr. 
Donovan moved to continue to the 10/8 meeting. Mr. Dufromont seconded. In favor: Doyle, Donovan, 
Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. 
 
Public Hearing 
Notice of Intent (DEP File # 316-tba) 
Applicant: George Sarris 
Property Location: 234 Calvary Street 
Project Description: Raze an existing commercial building and a garage and construct a new 
commercial building within the same building footprint. The entire lot is within the 100-year floodplain 
and 200’ Riverfront Area. 
The applicant was present. Bob Bibbo of Bibbo Brothers presented for the applicant. Mr. Bibbo 
summarized the project. It is in floodplain and riverfront area. He noted the existing septic system, 
which will be removed. They will demolish both structures (building and garage) and rebuild the main 
building in almost the same footprint (about 40 sq.ft. larger). He showed a slight increase in 
compensatory flood storage based on the removal of the garage (it will not be rebuilt). The new 
building will have flood gates, so if water ever gets that high it will flow through. The septic will be 
filled with sand. They have an easement to connect to water and sewer on Calvary Street. They will 
be installing 10 galleys for storm water. Ms. Abbott noted that DEP hasn’t assigned a file number (so 
no decision can be made tonight). DEP has made technical comments and both Ms. Abbott and Mr. 
Bibbo have communicated with DEP about them. The applicant submitted some DEP-requested 
changes this afternoon; Ms. Abbott and DEP have not yet reviewed. Ms. Abbott recommends
Approved 10-8-2026 
continuing to the next meeting. She stated these are technical issues which can be worked out. Mr. 
Dufromont asked about the planned erosion controls and materials storage during demolition. Mr. 
Bibbo stated that standard erosion controls will be used and demolition material will be removed daily. 
He added that there will be no snow storage on site, per discussions with the conservation agent and 
MA DEP. There will also be no salt used. Mr. Dufromont asked about parking. There is parking now, 
and the specific number of parking spaces after completion will be worked out with the building 
department. Mr. Donovan commented on the septic vs. sewer change and had minor questions about 
the building location and size and the use of the easement [the parcel does not have direct street 
frontage and is accessed by an easement through 224 Calvary Street]. He asked about the building’s 
planned use. Mr. Bibbo noted that this has not been settled; acceptable uses will be worked out with 
the building department and zoning board. The owner plans to lease the space out. Heavy equipment 
will not be stored on site. Mr. Donovan asked if the building will be only one story. Mr. Bibbo 
confirmed this, although it might also have loft space. Plans have not been finalized. Mr. Doyle 
commented that this looked straightforward. He asked if the applicant had worked with the 
engineering department yet regarding storm water. Mr. Bibbo said they had not but are planning to.  
Mr. Donovan moved to continue to the 10/8 meeting; Mr. Fitzgerald seconded. Mr. Dufromont asked 
the applicant to confirm that this would be enough time; Mr. Bibbo thinks so, but will inform the 
commission if more time will be needed. In favor: Doyle, Donovan, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion 
passed. 
 
Commission Business 
• Approval of meeting minutes from 9- 10-2026. Mr. Donovan so moved, seconded by Mr. 
Dufromont. In favor: Doyle, Donovan, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. 
 
Correspondence 
• NOTED: MA DEP reminds  all ConComs that drought status determinations are “backwards 
looking.” The Northeast Region (including Waltham) remains in drought and ConComs should 
not accept intermittent stream determinations made since 8/1/25 without additional investigation. 
 
Site Visit Reports 
• Lyman Estate. Ms. Abbott has a visit scheduled next week to inspect the new plantings (DEP 
316-0734). 
 
Committee Reports 
• Paine Estate Forest Management Plan subcommittee.  Mr. Dufromont noted they plan to meet 
with the city purchasing agent to discuss and work on a plan to move forward. 
• CPC: Met September 22.  Mr. Fitzgerald reported there were three funding requests: (1) First 
Parish Church steeple repairs, $50,768 for painting and repairs, mostly cosmetic work. 
Approved. (2) 20 Felton Street, community day center, for windows and siding replacement, 
$104,600, also supported by the historical commission as this is a 136-year old building. There 
is some urgency to the request due to the building condition and winter approaching. Approved, 
although a second request is expected as this covers only three sides of the building. (3) Gore 
Place, restoration of 43 windows, a large project, south side of the building only. $350,000 
requested, approved.  Brief discussion.  Mr. Fitzgerald also noted some discussion about the 
funds available to the CPC. Next meeting scheduled for 11/17. 
 
New Business 
• Mr. Daly from the commission office informed the commission that today the law department 
delivered 9 draft conservation restrictions for review. He and Ms. Abbott will work with the CPC 
staff to review and understand and note any concerns. He hopes that by either the 10/8 or the
Approved 10-8-2026 
10/22 meeting they will be able to give a recommendation to the commission for approval status. 
The CRs include not just 200 Trapelo Road (Fernald) but all parcels purchased with CPC funds. 
Some of these are not in WPA jurisdictional areas, so ConCom involvement is expected to be 
minimal for those. Mr. Doyle asked that the text of the CRs be made available to the commission 
for review. 
 
Motion to adjourn by Mr. Donovan, seconded by Mr. Dufromont. All present in favor. Motion passed. 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:30 PM.
